finding.claim: PUT /doc/<doc_id> overwrites the body of any document without an authorization check, because the can_edit result is discarded.
finding.source: Any caller of PUT /doc/<doc_id> (doc_id path segment and JSON body are attacker-controlled; caller identity is g.user).

trace.note: doc = DOCS[doc_id] loads the target document.
can_edit(g.user, doc) is called but its return value is ignored, so no abort occurs.

finding.guards_checked: can_edit (docs.py:7-8) has correct owner/editor logic but its result is unused here; require_edit (docs.py:11-13) would enforce it but is not called by this handler; no before_request, login decorator, or auth check in this file; update_title (docs.py:27) does enforce require_edit, so the two endpoints are inconsistent.

verdict.guard_found: none effective. can_edit (docs.py:7-8) returns a bool, but its result is discarded by the bare call at docs.py:19, so nothing aborts before the write at docs.py:20. require_edit (docs.py:11-13) is the enforcing variant, but update_doc does not call it; update_title at docs.py:27 does, which confirms the inconsistency. No before_request hook or login decorator appears in docs.py.
verdict.reason: update_doc at docs.py:19 calls can_edit(g.user, doc) as a bare statement, so its False result never reaches an abort, and docs.py:20 overwrites doc["body"] for any caller; the only assumption is that g.user is populated by authentication code outside this file, since nothing in docs.py sets it.

finding.claim: Authentication is not enforced in this file: g.user is read but never set here, so the authorization decision depends on an authentication layer that is not in the repository.
finding.source: Any unauthenticated request reaching the PUT handlers.
finding.sink: g.user reads in update_doc (docs.py:19) and update_title (docs.py:27)

trace.note: g.user is read as the actor for can_edit.
g.user is read as the actor for require_edit.

finding.guards_checked: No g.user assignment, login decorator, or before_request hook in docs.py. If g.user is unset, the handlers raise AttributeError (500). If middleware elsewhere sets it, that layer was not audited.

verdict.guard_found: None effective on update_doc. can_edit (docs.py:7-8) returns a bool, but the call at docs.py:19 is a bare statement whose result is discarded, so the body write at docs.py:20 always runs. require_edit (docs.py:11-13) does abort(403) on failure, and update_title calls it (docs.py:27), so update_title is guarded. No auth middleware, login decorator, or before_request hook exists in the repo.
verdict.reason: The trace lines at docs.py:19 and 27 are accurate, but the claim is misframed: update_doc's check at docs.py:19 is a discarded bool, so any user whose g.user is set by middleware outside this repo can overwrite any doc body via PUT /doc/<id>. Anonymous requests fail with AttributeError (500) rather than succeeding, so the attacker must be an authenticated low-privilege user, not "any unauthenticated request" as the source states.

finding.claim: Unknown document IDs raise an unhandled KeyError, which becomes a 500 and may leak a traceback when debug mode is enabled.
finding.source: Attacker-chosen doc_id path segment not present in DOCS.
finding.sink: DOCS[doc_id] lookups in update_doc (docs.py:18) and update_title (docs.py:26)

trace.note: DOCS[doc_id] raises KeyError for an unknown ID.

finding.guards_checked: No DOCS.get or abort(404) handling in either handler.

verdict.guard_found: none. No DOCS.get, no try/except, no 404 abort, and no app errorhandler. The lookup at docs.py:18 and docs.py:26 runs before any ownership check, so an unknown doc_id raises KeyError first.
verdict.reason: An anonymous client can send PUT /doc/<unknown-id>, and DOCS[doc_id] at docs.py:18 (and docs.py:26) raises an uncaught KeyError before any authorization runs, so Flask returns a 500 and, with debug enabled, a traceback. The claim is accurate but low severity: it is a robustness bug (404 expected), with information disclosure only in debug mode. Separately, docs.py:19 calls can_edit(g.user, doc) as a bare statement and discards the result, so update_doc has no authorization check at all. That is a more serious issue than the one under review and should be reported separately.
